name: to_sparse_csc
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::to_sparse_csc(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest defines the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must not be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::to_sparse_csc(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. Semantics: converts a dense tensor (or an accepted sparse source) to CSC layout, returning a torch.sparse_csc tensor whose ccol_indices, row_indices and values reproduce the native result; dense_dim selects how many trailing extents form the dense tail, the schema default is None (JSON null), which the test fixtures treat as 0, with valid values in [0, rank - 2]. The tests call the operator as torch.ops.aten.to_sparse_csc(input) and torch.ops.aten.to_sparse_csc(input, dense_dim) against flag_gems.to_sparse_csc, and additionally require: rank < 2 raises IndexError; the parametrized non-int dense_dim values [1.5, "0", [0]] raise RuntimeError or TypeError; dense_dim outside [0, rank - 2] raises RuntimeError; a non-tensor input raises RuntimeError or TypeError; a zero batch product raises RuntimeError while an empty matrix extent is legal; a quantized source raises RuntimeError, and a blocked-sparse (BSR) source raises RuntimeError in the runs where that case is collected, which requires the runtime's static int64 support flag. Mutation/aliasing: the conversion is read-only, so the operand and its parent storage are unchanged; for an input that is already a CSC tensor the pytest asserts the result is the same object as the source tensor (assert res_out is res_src), which is input-dependent behavior described here rather than a modeled conditional effect. The dense_dim default was rendered as JSON null from the ATen string default None (Optional[int]).
